# Figures: Screens

<!-- Generated by `npm run figures:docs` from src/components/figures/catalog.ts. Edit the catalogue, then run it again. -->

What does the product look like, step by step? Screenshots with a job: a walkthrough that counts steps and minutes, a screen with numbered notes, a before and after, products side by side.

How to add one to an entry, and the rules they all follow: [figures.md](../figures.md).

In this file: [Shot](#shot) · [ScreenSteps](#screensteps) · [BeforeAfter](#beforeafter) · [Compare](#compare) · [Anatomy](#anatomy)

## Shot

`S-01` · One screenshot in a browser or phone frame, with numbered pins and a note for each.

**Use it for**

- Review, "What works" and "Where it loses people": one screen, two or three things to see on it.
- Observation, "What I saw": the screen that prompted it.

**Not for:** A sequence of screens: use ScreenSteps. More than five pins: the screen is doing too much for one figure.

**Skills Map:** territories experience, activation; skills `visual-hierarchy`, `affordances`, `empty-states`, `interface-feedback`, `landing-experience`, `microcopy`, `trust-signals`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`src`** `string`: Path of the screenshot, under `/img/fieldwork/<entry>/`. Leave out to draw a placeholder that names the missing screenshot.
- **`alt`** *(required)* `string`: What the screenshot shows. Also the text of the placeholder.
- **`frame`** `'browser' | 'phone' | 'none'`: Default "browser".
- **`url`** `string`: Shown in the browser bar.
- **`ratio`** `string`: CSS aspect ratio of the visible area, "16 / 10". The image is cropped from the top to fit.
- **`pins`** `{ x: number; y: number; note?: string; kind?: 'note' | 'friction' | 'value' }[]`: `x` and `y` are percentages from the left and top of the screenshot. `friction` is pink, `value` yellow.
- **`width`** `number`: Width of the image file in pixels. With `height`, the page does not jump while the image loads.
- **`height`** `number`: Height of the image file in pixels.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Shot
  title="The landing page says one thing and offers one action"
  src="/img/figures/d-home.webp"
  alt="The landing page of productengineer.pro"
  url="productengineer.pro"
  ratio="16 / 10"
  pins={[
    {
      x: 89,
      y: 25,
      kind: 'value',
      note: 'The promise is in the reader’s terms: see where you stand.',
    },
    {
      x: 29,
      y: 62,
      note: 'One primary action. The second button is for people who would rather not choose.',
    },
    { x: 80, y: 74, note: 'The numbers are the claim: 350 skills on one map.' },
  ]}
  evidence="observed"
  source="Development build, 1280 px wide, 13 Nov 2026"
/>
```

## ScreenSteps

`S-02` · A walkthrough, screen by screen. It counts screens, seconds and decisions before the first moment of value.

**Use it for**

- Review, "First run": the path from the landing page to the first moment of value.
- Experiment and improvement, "What I built" and "What I shipped": the new path, step by step.

**Not for:** Screens that are not a sequence. For two versions of one screen use BeforeAfter.

**Skills Map:** territories activation, experience; skills `first-run-flows`, `signup-flow`, `step-reduction`, `aha-moments`, `first-successful-task`, `user-flows`, `task-analysis`, `guided-setup`, `decision-friction`

**Motion:** reveal, interactive

**Props**

- **`steps`** *(required)* `{ title: string; src?: string; alt?: string; note?: string; time?: number; kind?: 'step' | 'decision' | 'friction' | 'value'; pins?: Pin[] }[]`: `time` is seconds since the first screen. `decision`: the person must choose before getting anything. `friction`: where it loses people. `value`: the first moment it pays off (mark one). Without `src` a placeholder is drawn.
- **`frame`** `'browser' | 'phone' | 'none'`: Default "phone".
- **`ratio`** `string`: CSS aspect ratio of every screen, "9 / 19".
- **`layout`** `'strip' | 'stack'`: `strip` (default) scrolls sideways. `stack` puts one step per row, with room for longer notes.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<ScreenSteps
  title="A first run of this site on a phone"
  frame="phone"
  ratio="9 / 18.5"
  steps={[
    {
      title: 'Landing page',
      src: '/img/figures/p1-home.webp',
      time: 0,
      note: 'Says what it is and who it is for.',
    },
    {
      title: 'The Skills Map',
      src: '/img/figures/p2-atlas.webp',
      time: 8,
      note: 'The whole map at once. Nothing to fill in.',
    },
    {
      title: 'A territory',
      src: '/img/figures/p3-territory.webp',
      time: 21,
      note: 'Its question, then its capabilities.',
    },
    {
      title: 'A skill',
      src: '/img/figures/p4-skill.webp',
      time: 40,
      kind: 'decision',
      note: 'Where do I stand on this one?',
    },
    {
      title: 'Marked as learning',
      src: '/img/figures/p5-status.webp',
      time: 52,
      kind: 'value',
      note: 'One tap, saved in the browser. No account asked.',
    },
    {
      title: 'Account',
      src: '/img/figures/p6-me.webp',
      time: 70,
      note: 'Optional, for a second device.',
    },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
  source="Screens from the development build; the times are example values"
/>
```

**Example: Stack layout, with placeholders while the screenshots are missing**

```mdx
<ScreenSteps
  frame="browser"
  layout="stack"
  steps={[
    {
      title: 'Pricing page',
      alt: 'Pricing page with three plans',
      kind: 'decision',
      note: 'Three plans to choose from before seeing the product.',
    },
    {
      title: 'Sign-up form',
      alt: 'Sign-up form with six fields',
      kind: 'friction',
      note: 'Six fields. Nothing has been shown yet.',
    },
    {
      title: 'First project',
      alt: 'A project with sample data',
      kind: 'value',
      note: 'Sample data, so the first screen is not empty.',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## BeforeAfter

`S-03` · Two versions of one screen under a slider.

**Use it for**

- Improvement, "What I shipped": the screen before and after.
- Experiment, "What I built": control and variant.

**Not for:** Screens with different layouts: put two Shots one after the other.

**Skills Map:** territories experience, shipping; skills `product-changes`, `friction-reduction`, `form-friction`, `visual-hierarchy`, `responsive-design`, `release-communication`

**Motion:** interactive

**Props**

- **`before`** *(required)* `{ src?: string; alt?: string; label?: string }`: Left side. `label` defaults to "Before".
- **`after`** *(required)* `{ src?: string; alt?: string; label?: string }`: Right side. `label` defaults to "After".
- **`ratio`** `string`: CSS aspect ratio of the frame. Default "16 / 10". Both images are cropped from the top.
- **`start`** `number`: Where the divider starts, 0 to 100. Default 50.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<BeforeAfter
  title="The map on a first visit and after marking what you know"
  before={{
    src: '/img/figures/d-map-before.webp',
    alt: 'The home page map with no skills marked',
    label: 'First visit',
  }}
  after={{
    src: '/img/figures/d-map-after.webp',
    alt: 'The same map with 120 skills marked',
    label: 'After marking',
  }}
  ratio="16 / 10"
  caption="Drag the divider. The map is the same; the tiles carry the progress."
  evidence="observed"
  source="Development build, 13 Nov 2026"
/>
```

## Compare

`S-04` · Products side by side on the same questions: words, numbers, yes or no, ratings.

**Use it for**

- Comparison, "Side by side": the table the section is built on.
- Review, "Trade-offs", against the obvious alternative.

**Not for:** One measure only (Bars), or pass and fail across many cases (CheckGrid).

**Skills Map:** territories discovery, strategy; skills `competitive-analysis`, `substitutes`, `category-conventions`, `differentiation`, `packaging`, `pricing`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`subjects`** *(required)* `string[]`: Column heads: the products compared.
- **`rows`** *(required)* `{ label: string; values: (string | number | boolean | null)[]; best?: number; note?: string; unit?: string; scale?: number }[]`: One value per subject. `true` and `false` draw yes and no; a number with `scale` draws a rating; `null` means not looked at. `best` is the index of the subject that does best.
- **`highlight`** `number`: Index of the subject to mark: your product, or the one the entry is about.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Compare
  title="The first lesson in three language apps"
  subjects={['App A', 'App B', 'Etengabe']}
  highlight={2}
  rows={[
    { label: 'Lesson before account', values: [true, false, false], best: 0 },
    { label: 'Screens to first exercise', values: [4, 9, 14], unit: 'screens', best: 0 },
    { label: 'Time to first exercise', values: ['0:35', '1:50', '2:40'] },
    { label: 'Explains the method', values: [1, 3, 2], scale: 3, best: 1 },
    { label: 'Asks for', values: ['Language', 'Email, language, level', 'Email, password, level'] },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
  source="Example values"
/>
```

## Anatomy

`S-05` · A piece of text taken apart: marked parts in the text, what each one does in the list.

**Use it for**

- AI work: a prompt or a context window, part by part.
- Content design: a line of microcopy, an error message, a landing-page headline, an email.

**Skills Map:** territories ai, experience, distribution; skills `prompt-context-engineering`, `structured-outputs`, `microcopy`, `plain-language`, `instructional-copy`, `product-terminology`, `messaging`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`parts`** *(required)* `{ text: string; label?: string; note?: string; kind?: 'ink' | 'signal' | 'lit' }[]`: The text in order. Parts with a `label` are marked and listed; parts without are plain. Line breaks in `text` are kept. `signal` is the part to look at, `lit` the part that works.
- **`as`** `'copy' | 'prompt'`: `prompt` sets it in monospace. Default "copy".

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example: A prompt**

```mdx
<Anatomy
  title="The prompt behind the first-run audit"
  as="prompt"
  parts={[
    {
      text: 'You review first-run flows of web apps.',
      label: 'Role',
      note: 'Narrows the vocabulary the model reaches for.',
    },
    { text: '\n\n' },
    {
      text: 'List every point where the user must decide something before getting anything back.',
      label: 'Task',
      kind: 'signal',
      note: 'One job. The first version asked for three.',
    },
    { text: '\n\n' },
    {
      text: 'Use only what is in the screenshots. If a step is not shown, say so.',
      label: 'Constraint',
      kind: 'lit',
      note: 'The line that stopped invented steps.',
    },
    { text: '\n\n' },
    {
      text: 'Answer as JSON: [{ "step": number, "decision": string }]',
      label: 'Output',
      note: 'The next step parses it, so no prose.',
    },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
/>
```

**Example: Interface copy**

```mdx
<Anatomy
  parts={[
    {
      text: 'Create your account',
      label: 'Heading',
      kind: 'signal',
      note: 'Says what the form does, not what the learner gets.',
    },
    { text: ' to ' },
    {
      text: 'keep your progress',
      label: 'Benefit',
      kind: 'lit',
      note: 'The reason to sign up. It should come first.',
    },
    { text: '. ' },
    {
      text: 'It takes a minute.',
      label: 'Cost',
      note: 'Sets the expectation before the fields appear.',
    },
  ]}
/>
```
